376	pub fn fold_journal_to_snapshot(
377	    events: &[crate::orch::OrchEvent],
378	    scalars: &JournalScalars,
379	) -> Result<TaskProgressSnapshot, BridgeError> {
380	    let mut checkpoints = Vec::new();
381	    let mut starts: Vec<(NodeId, i64)> = Vec::new();
382	
383	    for event in events {
384	        match &event.kind {
385	            crate::orch::OrchEventKind::NodeStarted { node } => {
386	                let node = NodeId::parse(node)?;
387	                starts.retain(|(started, _seq)| started != &node);
388	                starts.push((node, event.seq));
389	            }
390	            crate::orch::OrchEventKind::NodeFinished {
391	                node,
392	                ok,
393	                output,
394	                usage: _,
395	            } => {
396	                let node = NodeId::parse(node)?;
397	                starts.retain(|(started, _seq)| started != &node);
398	                checkpoints.push((node, output.clone(), *ok, event.seq));
399	            }
400	            crate::orch::OrchEventKind::Terminal { .. } => {
401	                starts.clear();
402	            }
403	            crate::orch::OrchEventKind::Progress { .. }
404	            | crate::orch::OrchEventKind::Usage { .. }
405	            | crate::orch::OrchEventKind::Plan { .. }
406	            | crate::orch::OrchEventKind::ToolCall { .. }
407	            | crate::orch::OrchEventKind::ToolCallUpdate { .. } => {}
408	        }
409	    }
410	
411	    // `cut_seq` is trusted verbatim from the tasks-row scalar (= `last_event_seq`), NOT clamped to
412	    // the max event seq. This relies on the load-bearing dual-store invariant: every sequenced
413	    // writer bumps `last_event_seq` THEN inserts its journal row at `seq == last_event_seq` in the
414	    // SAME transaction (SQLite) / under the SAME guard (Memory), so `cut_seq >= max journal seq`
415	    // always holds. A future writer that journals WITHOUT bumping `last_event_seq` would break this.
416	    Ok(TaskProgressSnapshot {
417	        status: scalars.status,
418	        result: scalars.result.clone(),
419	        error: scalars.error.clone(),
420	        checkpoints,
421	        starts,
422	        terminal_seq: scalars.terminal_seq,
423	        cut_seq: scalars.cut_seq,
424	    })
425	}

977	    async fn progress_snapshot(&self, task: &TaskId) -> Result<TaskProgressSnapshot, BridgeError> {
978	        let row = {
979	            let g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();
980	            g.get(task.as_str())
981	                .cloned()
982	                .ok_or(BridgeError::StoreFailure)?
983	        };
984	        let cut_seq = {
985	            let g = self.seq_counters.lock().unwrap();
986	            *g.get(task.as_str()).unwrap_or(&0)
987	        };
988	        let terminal_seq = {
989	            let g = self.terminal_seqs.lock().unwrap();
990	            g.get(task.as_str()).copied()
991	        };
992	        let mut checkpoints: Vec<(NodeId, String, bool, i64)> = {
993	            let g = self.checkpoints.lock().unwrap();
994	            let mut out = Vec::new();
995	            for ((tid, nid), (output, ok, _ts, seq, _usage)) in g.iter() {
996	                if tid == task.as_str() {
997	                    let node = NodeId::parse(nid).map_err(|_| BridgeError::StoreFailure)?;
998	                    out.push((node, output.clone(), *ok, *seq));
999	                }
1000	            }
1001	            out
1002	        };
1003	        checkpoints.sort_by_key(|(_n, _o, _ok, seq)| *seq);
1004	        let starts: Vec<(NodeId, i64)> = {
1005	            let g = self.starts.lock().unwrap();
1006	            let mut out = Vec::new();
1007	            for ((tid, nid), (seq, _ts)) in g.iter() {
1008	                if tid == task.as_str() {
1009	                    let node = NodeId::parse(nid).map_err(|_| BridgeError::StoreFailure)?;
1010	                    out.push((node, *seq));
1011	                }
1012	            }
1013	            out
1014	        };
1015	        // Ensure cut_seq >= every seq actually included in the snapshot.  Under the
1016	        // single-writer-per-task model this is almost always a no-op, but a concurrent
1017	        // write between the counter read and the data reads could otherwise produce a
1018	        // snapshot where a checkpoint or start seq exceeds the recorded cut_seq.
1019	        let max_included = checkpoints
1020	            .iter()
1021	            .map(|(_, _, _, s)| *s)
1022	            .chain(starts.iter().map(|(_, s)| *s))
1023	            .chain(terminal_seq)
1024	            .max()
1025	            .unwrap_or(0);
1026	        let cut_seq = cut_seq.max(max_included);
1027	        Ok(TaskProgressSnapshot {
1028	            status: row.status,
1029	            result: row.result,
1030	            error: row.error,
1031	            checkpoints,
1032	            starts,
1033	            terminal_seq,
1034	            cut_seq,
1035	        })
1036	    }
